package api

import "time"

// TrailReviewStartRequest is the body for POST /api/v1/trails/{trail_id}/reviews.
type TrailReviewStartRequest struct {
	HeadSHA *string `json:"head_sha,omitempty"`
	BaseSHA *string `json:"base_sha,omitempty"`
	BaseRef *string `json:"base_ref,omitempty"`
	HeadRef *string `json:"head_ref,omitempty"`
}

// TrailReviewStartResponse is returned after creating or reusing a code review.
type TrailReviewStartResponse struct {
	ReviewID       string                 `json:"review_id"`
	TrailID        string                 `json:"trail_id"`
	RepositoryID   string                 `json:"repository_id"`
	CodeVersionID  string                 `json:"code_version_id"`
	BaseSHA        *string                `json:"base_sha"`
	HeadSHA        *string                `json:"head_sha"`
	EventStreamURL string                 `json:"event_stream_url"`
	DiffURL        string                 `json:"diff_url"`
	FilesURL       string                 `json:"files_url"`
	Limits         TrailReviewStartLimits `json:"limits"`
}

// TrailReviewStartLimits describes per-review API limits.
type TrailReviewStartLimits struct {
	MaxCommentsPerBatch int `json:"max_comments_per_batch"`
}

// TrailReviewStateResponse is returned by GET /api/v1/trails/{trail_id}/reviews/{id}.
type TrailReviewStateResponse struct {
	Review      TrailReview            `json:"review"`
	CodeVersion TrailReviewCodeVersion `json:"code_version"`
	Counts      TrailReviewCounts      `json:"counts"`
	Comments    []TrailReviewComment   `json:"comments"`
	NextCursor  *string                `json:"next_cursor"`
	EventCursor string                 `json:"event_cursor"`
}

// TrailReview represents a review session.
type TrailReview struct {
	ID            string    `json:"id"`
	TrailID       string    `json:"trail_id"`
	CodeVersionID string    `json:"code_version_id"`
	ActorID       string    `json:"actor_id"`
	Summary       *string   `json:"summary"`
	StartedAt     time.Time `json:"started_at"`
}

// TrailReviewCodeVersion pins the base/head that a review covers.
type TrailReviewCodeVersion struct {
	ID           string    `json:"id"`
	TrailID      string    `json:"trail_id"`
	RepositoryID string    `json:"repository_id"`
	BaseRef      *string   `json:"base_ref"`
	HeadRef      *string   `json:"head_ref"`
	BaseSHA      *string   `json:"base_sha"`
	HeadSHA      *string   `json:"head_sha"`
	CapturedAt   time.Time `json:"captured_at"`
}

// TrailReviewCounts are review-scoped comment counts.
type TrailReviewCounts struct {
	Open      int `json:"open"`
	Resolved  int `json:"resolved"`
	Dismissed int `json:"dismissed"`
	Stale     int `json:"stale"`
	Total     int `json:"total"`
}

// TrailReviewCommentsResponse is returned by trail/review comment list endpoints.
type TrailReviewCommentsResponse struct {
	Comments   []TrailReviewComment `json:"comments"`
	HasMore    bool                 `json:"has_more"`
	NextOffset *int                 `json:"next_offset"`
}

// TrailReviewComment is a single agent-native review finding.
type TrailReviewComment struct {
	ID                        string                       `json:"id"`
	TrailID                   string                       `json:"trail_id"`
	RepositoryID              string                       `json:"repository_id"`
	ReviewID                  string                       `json:"review_id"`
	CodeVersionID             string                       `json:"code_version_id"`
	ActorID                   string                       `json:"actor_id"`
	Title                     *string                      `json:"title"`
	Body                      *string                      `json:"body"`
	Severity                  *string                      `json:"severity"`
	Confidence                *float64                     `json:"confidence"`
	Status                    string                       `json:"status"`
	StatusReason              *string                      `json:"status_reason"`
	StaleOutcome              string                       `json:"stale_outcome"`
	StaleCheckedAt            *time.Time                   `json:"stale_checked_at"`
	StaleCheckedCodeVersionID *string                      `json:"stale_checked_code_version_id"`
	ClientID                  *string                      `json:"client_id"`
	ClientIDHash              *string                      `json:"client_id_hash"`
	CreatedAt                 time.Time                    `json:"created_at"`
	UpdatedAt                 time.Time                    `json:"updated_at"`
	Location                  TrailReviewLocation          `json:"location"`
	SuggestedChanges          []TrailReviewSuggestedChange `json:"suggested_changes,omitempty"`
	ThreadID                  *string                      `json:"thread_id,omitempty"`
	ThreadMessageCount        int                          `json:"thread_message_count,omitempty"`
	OutgoingLinks             []TrailReviewOutgoingLink    `json:"outgoing_links,omitempty"`
}

// TrailReviewLocation identifies where a finding applies.
type TrailReviewLocation struct {
	ID              string  `json:"id"`
	ReviewCommentID string  `json:"review_comment_id"`
	CodeVersionID   string  `json:"code_version_id"`
	Granularity     string  `json:"granularity"`
	FilePath        *string `json:"file_path"`
	StartLine       *int    `json:"start_line"`
	StartColumn     *int    `json:"start_column"`
	EndLine         *int    `json:"end_line"`
	EndColumn       *int    `json:"end_column"`
	SelectedText    *string `json:"selected_text"`
	NearbyText      *string `json:"nearby_text"`
	Language        *string `json:"language"`
}

// TrailReviewSuggestedChange describes a machine-applicable or manual fix.
type TrailReviewSuggestedChange struct {
	ID                string    `json:"id"`
	ReviewCommentID   string    `json:"review_comment_id"`
	CodeVersionID     string    `json:"code_version_id"`
	ChangeType        string    `json:"change_type"`
	Patch             *string   `json:"patch"`
	Instruction       *string   `json:"instruction"`
	ExpectedFilePath  *string   `json:"expected_file_path"`
	ExpectedFileHash  *string   `json:"expected_file_hash"`
	ExpectedStartLine *int      `json:"expected_start_line"`
	ExpectedEndLine   *int      `json:"expected_end_line"`
	ExpectedLines     *string   `json:"expected_lines"`
	CreatedBy         string    `json:"created_by"`
	CreatedAt         time.Time `json:"created_at"`
	UpdatedAt         time.Time `json:"updated_at"`
}

// TrailReviewOutgoingLink relates two review comments.
type TrailReviewOutgoingLink struct {
	SourceCommentID string `json:"source_comment_id"`
	TargetCommentID string `json:"target_comment_id"`
	LinkType        string `json:"link_type"`
}

// TrailReviewCommentPatchRequest updates a review finding.
type TrailReviewCommentPatchRequest struct {
	Title        *string  `json:"title,omitempty"`
	Body         *string  `json:"body,omitempty"`
	Severity     *string  `json:"severity,omitempty"`
	Confidence   *float64 `json:"confidence,omitempty"`
	Status       string   `json:"status,omitempty"`
	StatusReason *string  `json:"status_reason,omitempty"`
}

// TrailSubmitReviewRequest is the body for POST /api/v1/trails/{host}/{owner}/{repo}/{number}/review.
type TrailSubmitReviewRequest struct {
	Event string `json:"event"`
	Body  string `json:"body,omitempty"`
}

// TrailSubmitReviewResponse is returned after approving or requesting changes on a trail.
type TrailSubmitReviewResponse struct {
	OK     bool              `json:"ok"`
	Review TrailSubmitReview `json:"review"`
}

// TrailSubmitReview is a human trail review verdict.
type TrailSubmitReview struct {
	ID        string    `json:"id"`
	Author    string    `json:"author"`
	Event     string    `json:"event"`
	Body      *string   `json:"body"`
	CommitSHA string    `json:"commit_sha"`
	CreatedAt time.Time `json:"created_at"`
}

Flags: `--status`, `--severity`, `--stale`, `--include-dismissed`, `--limit/-n`, `--offset`, `--json`. ```text Trail #42 Add token refresh Status: in_review Branch: feat/token-refresh Base: main ID: trl_123 Open findings: 3 high 1 medium 1 low 1 Resolved: 2 Dismissed: 1 Stale: 0 High H src/auth/session.ts:88 cmt_high_123 Missing expiry skew handling Medium M src/api/client.ts:141 cmt_med_456 Retry loop can spin forever Low L src/ui/Login.tsx:52 cmt_low_789 Error state is swallowed Actions: entire trail review show entire trail review apply --resolve entire trail review resolve -m "fixed in " entire trail review dismiss -m "not applicable" entire trail review watch ``` If the filtered page is empty: ```text No review findings match the current filters. ``` With `--json`, output is an object containing `trail`, `counts`, `comments`, and `has_more`. ### `entire trail review comments []` Lists review findings. Flags: `--status`, `--severity`, `--stale`, `--include-dismissed`, `--limit/-n`, `--offset`, `--json`. ```text ID SEV STATUS LOCATION TITLE cmt_high_123 high open src/auth/session.ts:88 Missing expiry skew handling cmt_med_456 medium open src/api/client.ts:141 Retry loop can spin forever ``` When more pages exist: ```text More findings available; rerun with --offset for the next page. ``` When no findings match: ```text No review findings found. ``` With `--json`, output is the same object shape as `entire trail review --json`. ### `entire trail review show [] ` Shows one finding. Prefix matching is supported when unambiguous. ```text Comment: cmt_high_123 Review: rvw_123 Status: open Severity: high Confidence: 0.94 Location: src/auth/session.ts:88 Title: Missing expiry skew handling Token refresh should allow clock skew before treating the session as expired. Suggested changes: - sug_123 (unified_diff) file: src/auth/session.ts patch: diff --git a/src/auth/session.ts b/src/auth/session.ts ... ``` ### `entire trail review start []` Starts an agent-native review for the trail via `POST /api/v1/trails/{trail_id}/reviews` and sends an `Idempotency-Key` based on trail/base/head inputs. Flags: `--base-ref`, `--head-ref`, `--base-sha`, `--head-sha`, `--json`, `--watch`. ```text Started review rvw_123 for trail #42 (Add token refresh) Code version: cv_123 Base: 1a2b3c4d5e6f Head: 9f8e7d6c5b4a Next: entire trail review watch 42 entire trail review comments 42 ``` With `--json`, output is the API start response, including `review_id`, `trail_id`, `code_version_id`, base/head SHAs, URLs, and limits. With `--watch`, the command starts the review and then enters the same output mode as `entire trail review watch`. ### `entire trail review watch []` Streams trail review SSE events. Flags: `--json`, `--show-pings`, `--once`. Human output starts with the watch banner on stderr and stream events on stdout: ```text Watching trail #42 (gh/entireio/cli, id trl_123) — Ctrl+C to stop ● connected to trail trl_123 after event 17 [12:34:56] session started by agent:reviewer (code version cv_123) [12:35:04] comment created by agent:reviewer on src/auth/session.ts (high) — cmt_high_123 [12:35:10] session ended by agent:reviewer (done) ``` With `--json`, each SSE event is emitted as one JSON line: ```json {"event":"comment.created","data":{"id":"18","trail_id":"trl_123","event_type":"comment.created"}} ``` ### `entire trail review apply [] ` Applies supported `unified_diff` suggested changes. Safety behavior: - verifies current `HEAD` matches the reviewed head when the API provides one - rejects absolute paths, repository escapes, and `.git` metadata paths - concatenates all supported unified-diff patches, checks once, then applies once atomically Flags: `--check`, `--resolve`. Successful apply: ```text Applied 1 suggested change(s). ``` Successful check-only run: ```text 1 suggested change(s) apply cleanly. ``` With `--resolve`: ```text Applied 1 suggested change(s). Updated comment cmt_high_123: open → resolved ``` Unsupported suggestion types are skipped before applying supported patches: ```text Skipping suggested change sug_manual (manual_instruction): only unified_diff patches are supported. ``` ### `entire trail review resolve [] ` Marks a finding resolved. Flags: `--message/-m`. ```text Updated comment cmt_high_123: open → resolved ``` If `--message` is omitted, the status reason defaults to `Resolved via Entire CLI`. ### `entire trail review dismiss [] ` Marks a finding dismissed. Flags: `--message/-m`. ```text Updated comment cmt_low_789: open → dismissed ``` If `--message` is omitted, the status reason defaults to `Dismissed via Entire CLI`. ### `entire trail review reopen [] ` Reopens a finding. Flags: `--message/-m`. ```text Updated comment cmt_low_789: dismissed → open ``` If `--message` is omitted, the status reason defaults to `Reopened via Entire CLI`. ### `entire trail review approve []` Submits an `APPROVE` verdict on the trail. Flags: `--message/-m`. ```text APPROVE submitted by dipree on 9f8e7d6c5b4a ``` ### `entire trail review request-changes []` Submits a `REQUEST_CHANGES` verdict on the trail. content.text:
I fetched PR #1266 locally. High-level: it’s a big, useful integration, but it front-loads too much product/API complexity into the CLI: a 1.2k-line command file handles target resolution, API paths, pagination, hydration, dashboard aggregation, status mutation, review submission, SSE delegation, patch safety, and git apply.

## Main concerns

- **Scope is too wide for one CLI integration**
  - Dashboard/list/show
  - Start/watch
  - Resolve/dismiss/reopen
  - Approve/request-changes
  - Apply server-provided patches safely  
  These are multiple feature slices, not one integration.

- **CLI is compensating for missing API shape**
  - Dashboard counts require fetching *all* comments separately.
  - `show/apply/resolve` must scan paginated comments to find a comment ID, then fetch review state to hydrate suggestions.
  - Pagination ignores `NextOffset` and assumes `offset += limit`.
  - A direct comment detail/update endpoint would remove a lot of client code.

- **Patch apply is the highest-risk part**
  - It adds git HEAD checks, custom patch path validation, atomic apply logic, and temp repo tests.
  - Even with current hardening, path validation is subtle across quoted paths, case-insensitive filesystems, symlinks, etc.
  - This is probably not needed for the first CLI version.

- **Some UX combinations are awkward**
  - `trail review start --json --watch` prints JSON then enters human watch mode.
  - `--status`, `--stale`, and `--include-dismissed` create confusing combinations.
  - `trail watch` and `trail review watch` duplicate the same behavior.

## Best simplification options

### Option 1: MVP cut
Ship only:

```text
entire trail review [number]
entire trail review comments [number]
entire trail review show [number] <comment-id>
entire trail review start [number]
entire trail review watch [number]
```

Defer:

```text
apply
resolve/dismiss/reopen
approve/request-changes
```

This likely removes the riskiest 30–40% of the PR, especially patch application.

### Option 2: Move orchestration server-side
Add API endpoints shaped for the CLI:

```text
GET /trails/{id}/reviews/dashboard
GET /trails/{id}/reviews/comments/{comment_id}
PATCH /trails/{id}/reviews/comments/{comment_id}
```

Then the CLI avoids:
- scanning all comments for prefix matches
- fetching review state just to hydrate one comment
- computing counts locally
- managing list pagination for dashboard totals

This preserves functionality while simplifying the client.

### Option 3: Keep features, but refactor structure
Split `trail_review_cmd.go` into smaller files:

```text
trail_review_cmd.go       cobra wiring only
trail_review_api.go       typed API calls/path builders
trail_review_print.go     rendering
trail_review_apply.go     patch/git apply logic
trail_review_target.go    shared trail resolution
```

Also add a shared JSON helper in `api.Client` to reduce repeated `Get/Post/Patch -> check -> decode` boilerplate.

### Option 4: Simplify UX flags
Replace the filter matrix with presets:

```text
--all
--closed
--stale
--severity high
```

instead of exposing `--status`, `--stale`, and `--include-dismissed` independently.

## My recommendation

For fastest safe merge: **ship the read/watch/start slice first**, drop `apply` and verdict submission from this PR, and add a server-side dashboard/comment-detail endpoint before reintroducing mutations. That would make this feel like a clean CLI integration instead of a full review client implemented in one command file.

But would also love to be able to create a review comment via API? I always see "entire trail review [number]" NUMBER but wtf. I want lists, no one knows a fucking number before not having a list to pick from?

content.text:
Yeah, agreed. The `[number]` UX is backwards.

Right now PR #1266 says:

```text
entire trail review [<number>]
```

but the discoverability path is weak because `entire trail list` currently prints branch/author/time, not the trail number/title. So users are asked for a number they probably have no way to know.

I’d change the integration around this:

## 1. Add a real review/trail list first

```text
entire trail review list
```

Example:

```text
NUM   STATUS      BRANCH                  TITLE                   OPEN  HIGH  UPDATED
425   in_review   feat/trail-review-cli   Add trail review CLI     6     2     1h ago
421   open        fix/auth-refresh        Fix token refresh        1     1     2d ago
```

Then:

```text
entire trail review 425
```

makes sense.

Also update `entire trail list` to include at least:

```text
NUM  STATUS  BRANCH  TITLE  UPDATED
```

If trail number is central to the CLI, every list must show it.

## 2. No args should list or pick

`entire trail review` should do:

1. If current branch has a trail: open that review dashboard.
2. Else if TTY: show an interactive picker.
3. Else: print the review list and say “pass a number”.

So the happy path is:

```text
entire trail review
```

not “go find a magic number first.”

## 3. Consider accepting more than numbers

Instead of only `[number]`, support a selector:

```text
entire trail review 425
entire trail review trl_abc123
entire trail review feat/trail-review-cli
```

Or explicit flags:

```text
entire trail review --number 425
entire trail review --id trl_abc123
entire trail review --branch feat/trail-review-cli
```

## 4. Yes: add create-comment API

This is missing from the integration. The CLI can read/review/apply, but agents need to **produce** review comments too.

I’d want an API like:

```http
POST /api/v1/trails/{trail_id}/reviews/{review_id}/comments
```

Body:

```json
{
  "client_id": "agent-run-123:finding-7",
  "title": "Missing expiry skew handling",
  "body": "Token refresh should allow clock skew before treating the session as expired.",
  "severity": "high",
  "confidence": 0.94,
  "location": {
    "file_path": "src/auth/session.ts",
    "start_line": 88,
    "end_line": 91
  },
  "suggested_changes": [
    {
      "change_type": "unified_diff",
      "patch": "diff --git a/src/auth/session.ts b/src/auth/session.ts\n..."
    }
  ]
}
```

Also probably batch:

```http
POST /api/v1/trails/{trail_id}/reviews/{review_id}/comments:batch
```

with idempotency via `client_id` / `Idempotency-Key`, because agents retry.

## My suggested simplification

For this PR, I’d prioritize:

```text
entire trail review list
entire trail review
entire trail review <number-or-id-or-branch>
entire trail review comments
entire trail review show <comment-id>
API: create review comment / batch create comments
```

Defer risky stuff like `apply`, `approve`, `request-changes`, maybe even status mutation. First make the loop discoverable and let agents create comments. Then layer mutations/apply on top.
Ok, but the user might already be on a branch within a repo that has a certain trail ID and so it would be good to just get them the comments for that or allow to post for that?

Yes — that should be the default path.

The CLI should treat “current branch’s trail” as the primary target, and trail number as an override.

Good UX:

```text
entire trail review
entire trail review comments
entire trail review comment add --file foo.go --line 42 --body "..."
```

All should resolve:

1. current git repo
2. current branch
3. trail for that branch
4. trail ID
5. latest/active review for that trail

Only if that fails should it ask for/list trails.

So I’d avoid advertising:

```text
entire trail review [number]
```

and instead frame it as:

```text
entire trail review [--trail <number|id|branch>]
```

Examples:

```text
entire trail review comments                 # current branch trail
entire trail review comments --trail 425     # explicit trail
entire trail review comments --trail trl_abc # explicit trail id
```

For posting comments, I’d add a trail-scoped API that does not force callers to know `review_id`:

```http
POST /api/v1/trails/{trail_id}/reviews/comments
```

Body:

```json
{
  "title": "Potential nil dereference",
  "body": "This can panic when user is nil.",
  "severity": "high",
  "location": {
    "file_path": "internal/auth/session.go",
    "start_line": 42
  }
}
```

Server can attach it to the active/latest review, or create/reuse one idempotently.

CLI:

```text
entire trail review comment add \
  --file internal/auth/session.go \
  --line 42 \
  --severity high \
  --title "Potential nil dereference" \
  --body "This can panic when user is nil."
```

For agents, also add batch:

```http
POST /api/v1/trails/{trail_id}/reviews/comments:batch
```

with `client_id` per finding for idempotency.

PR #1266 already partially does current-branch resolution when number is omitted, but the command shape/docs make the number feel central. I’d change the mental model to:

> “Current branch trail by default. List/pick only when ambiguous. Number/id/branch only as explicit override.”
Yes, exactly that. Make the relevant changes.

	cmd := &cobra.Command{

		Short: "Review a trail's agent findings",

Running 'entire trail review' shows the review dashboard for the current

trail in the same repo. Use 'entire trail review list' when you need to discover
a trail selector first.`,
		Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
			selector, err := parseOptionalTrailSelector(args, targetOpts.Selector)
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			return runTrailReviewDashboard(cmd, selector, opts)
		},
	}

	addTrailReviewListFlags(cmd, &opts)

	cmd.AddCommand(newTrailReviewListCmd())

	cmd.AddCommand(newTrailReviewCommentCmd(&targetOpts))

	return cmd
}

**Evaluating API considerations**

I’m considering whether adding the `truncateOneLine` dependency from `trail_review_cmd.go` to `trail_cmd.go` affects build tags. I'll need to inspect the trail list output and also consider the backend API endpoint for creating comments. The user mentioned wanting to create comments via API rather than just CLI, and that makes sense.

Maybe we should supporting direct POST for the API while ensuring that we can’t have a CLI “latest review” if no active review exists. I’ll also think about listing the “review list” with the current branch for clarity.

**Considering fallback for trails**

I've added the `review list`, but there’s a concern: we haven't implemented the option to list or pick when the current branch has no trail. The user mentioned it's frustrating not knowing the number before seeing the list. 

Should we add a fallback? Like, if there’s no current branch trail and no selector, we could print the list instead. 

Currently, `resolveTrailReviewTarget` returns an error if the branch is missing. Maybe for `runTrailReviewDashboard` and `runTrailReviewComments`, we could run the list if the selector is empty and an error occurs. The user really wants that list!

**Rethinking list default behavior**

I'm realizing that since "no one knows number before the list," the default should probably show the list. 

For the dashboard, maybe if the current branch has no trail, we should display the entire trail review. The existing root could fall back to the list as it does now, maybe mirroring the behavior. 

That would mean modifying the target resolution so that it doesn’t simply return an error. I could create an `authenticatedTrailReviewTarget` without output. In the runDashboard, I might check if there’s an error and if the selector is empty, handling the no-trail case gracefully!

Implemented the UX/API changes.

Changed:
- `entire trail review` now uses `[<trail>]` where trail can be number, id, or branch.
- Added persistent selector:
  - `--trail <number|id|branch>`
- Current branch remains the default target for:
  - `entire trail review`
  - `entire trail review comments`
  - `entire trail review comment add`
  - status/show/apply/watch/start/submit flows
- If `entire trail review` can’t find a current-branch trail, it now falls back to showing a repo trail list.
- Added:
  - `entire trail review list`
  - `entire trail review comment add`
  - `entire trail review comments add` alias
- Added trail-scoped create-comment API client path:
  - `POST /api/v1/trails/{trail_id}/reviews/comments`
- Added create request API types for review comments, locations, and suggested changes.
- Updated `entire trail list` rows to include `NUM`, `BRANCH`, `TITLE`, etc., so numbers are discoverable.
- Refactored watch slightly so review watch can stream by resolved trail ID, not just number.
- Added tests for selector parsing, review list output, create comment request building, and create-comment POST path.

Validation:
- `env -u PI_CODING_AGENT mise exec -- go test ./...` passed
- `mise exec -- golangci-lint run` passed
- `git diff --check` passed

Note: `git-remote-entire` is still untracked in the worktree; I left it untouched.

# E2E Tests

End-to-end tests for the `entire` CLI against real agents (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Codex, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI).

## Commands

```bash
mise run test:e2e [filter]                          # run filtered (or omit filter for all agents)
mise run test:e2e --agent claude-code [filter]       # Claude Code only
mise run test:e2e --agent gemini-cli [filter]        # Gemini CLI only
mise run test:e2e --agent opencode [filter]          # OpenCode only
mise run test:e2e --agent codex [filter]             # Codex only
mise run test:e2e --agent cursor [filter]            # Cursor only
mise run test:e2e --agent factoryai-droid [filter]   # Factory AI Droid only
mise run test:e2e --agent copilot-cli [filter]       # Copilot CLI only
go build ./...                                      # compile check (no agent CLI needed)
```

**Do NOT run E2E tests proactively.** They make real API calls that consume tokens and cost money. Only run when explicitly asked.

## Structure

```
e2e/
├── agents/       # Agent abstraction (Agent interface, tmux sessions, concurrency gates)
├── bootstrap/    # CI pre-test setup (auth config, warmup)
├── entire/       # `entire` CLI wrapper (enable, rewind, etc.)
├── exploratory/  # Experimental tests, not run by CI
├── tests/        # Blessed test files (run by CI)
└── testutil/     # Repo setup, assertions, artifact capture
```

## Key Patterns

- Every test uses `testutil.ForEachAgent` which runs it per registered agent with repo setup, concurrency gating, and timeout scaling.
- All operations go through `RepoState` (`s.RunPrompt`, `s.Git`) so they're logged to `console.log`.
- Use the `entire` package for CLI interactions, not raw `exec.Command`.
- Skip tests pending CLI fixes with `t.Skip("ENT-XXX: reason")`.

## Adding a New Agent

1. Create `agents/<name>.go` implementing the `Agent` interface.
2. Register it in `init()` with `Register(&YourAgent{})`.
3. Add a `Bootstrap()` method for any CI-specific setup (auth config, warmup).
4. Add a `RegisterGate("<name>", N)` call if concurrency needs limiting.
5. Ensure the agent name is accepted by `mise run test:e2e --agent <name>`.
6. Add the agent to `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` matrix and `e2e-isolated.yml` options.

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Description | Default |
|----------|-------------|---------|
| `E2E_AGENT` | Agent to test (`claude-code`, `gemini-cli`, `opencode`, `codex`, `cursor`, `factoryai-droid`, `copilot-cli`) | all registered |
| `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN` | Path to a pre-built `entire` binary | builds from source |
| `E2E_TIMEOUT` | Timeout per prompt | `2m` |
| `E2E_KEEP_REPOS` | Set to `1` to preserve temp repos after test | unset |
| `E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR` | Override artifact output directory | `e2e/artifacts/<timestamp>` |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Required for Claude Code | — |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | Required for Gemini CLI | — |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Required for Codex | — |
| `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` | Required for Copilot CLI (or `gh auth login`) | — |

## Debugging Failures

Artifacts are captured to `e2e/artifacts/` on every run (git-log, git-tree, console.log, checkpoint metadata, entire logs). Set `E2E_KEEP_REPOS=1` to preserve the temp repo — a symlink appears in the artifact dir pointing to it.

Use the `debug-e2e` skill (`.claude/skills/debug-e2e/`) for a structured workflow when investigating failures.

### Reading artifacts

- `console.log` — full operation transcript including agent stdout/stderr
- `git-log.txt` — commit history at time of failure
- `git-tree.txt` — working tree state
- `entire-logs/` — internal CLI logs

### Fixing flaky tests

When a test passes on retry but failed once, the problem is usually agent non-determinism, not a CLI bug. Common patterns:

- **Agent asked for confirmation instead of acting**: The model output contains "Does this look right?" or "Should I proceed?". Fix: append "Do not ask for confirmation, just make the change." to the prompt.
- **Agent wrote to wrong path or created extra files**: Fix: be more explicit about exact file paths and what _not_ to do.
- **Agent committed when it shouldn't have**: Fix: add "Do not commit" to the prompt.
- **Checkpoint wait timeout**: `WaitForCheckpoint` or `WaitForCheckpointAdvanceFrom` exceeded deadline. Fix: increase the timeout argument.

To diagnose: read `console.log` in the failing test's artifact directory. Compare what the agent actually did vs what the test expected.

## CI Workflows

- **`.github/workflows/e2e.yml`** — Runs full suite on push to main. Matrix: `[claude-code, opencode, gemini-cli, codex, cursor-cli, factoryai-droid, copilot-cli]`.
- **`.github/workflows/e2e-isolated.yml`** — Manual dispatch for debugging a single test. Inputs: agent + test name filter.

Both workflows run `go run ./e2e/bootstrap` before tests to handle agent-specific CI setup (auth config, warmup).

# Exploratory E2E Tests

Tests in this directory are **not run by CI**. They exist for:

- Validating bug fixes before the fix is merged (reference the Linear issue)
- Prototyping new test scenarios before promoting to `tests/`
- Reproducing reported issues

## Running

    go test -tags=e2e -count=1 -timeout=30m ./exploratory/...

## Promoting to blessed

Move the file to `tests/` — no other changes needed.

# Trail review CLI

`entire trail review` works on the trail for your current branch by default. You only need a selector when you want to operate on a different trail in the same repository.

A trail selector can be any of:

- trail number: `425` or `#425`
- trail id: `trl_abc123`
- branch name: `feat/token-refresh`

You can pass the selector positionally or with `--trail`:

```bash
entire trail review 425
entire trail review --trail feat/token-refresh
entire trail review comments --trail trl_abc123
```

If no current-branch trail can be resolved, `entire trail review` prints the repo trail list so you can pick one.

## Golden path

From a branch that already has a trail:

```bash
# 1. See review status for the current branch's trail.
entire trail review

# 2. Start/reuse an agent-native review for the current HEAD.
entire trail review start

# 3. List findings for the current branch's trail.
entire trail review comments

# 4. Create a review finding on the current branch's trail.
entire trail review comment add \
  --title "Missing expiry skew handling" \
  --body "Token refresh should allow clock skew before treating the session as expired." \
  --severity high \
  --confidence 0.94 \
  --file src/auth/session.ts \
  --line 88 \
  --client-id "agent-run-123:finding-7"

# 5. Inspect, resolve, or dismiss a finding.
entire trail review show <comment-id>
entire trail review resolve <comment-id> -m "fixed in <sha>"
entire trail review dismiss <comment-id> -m "not applicable"

# 6. Watch review events.
entire trail review watch
```

When you are not on the trail branch, discover and select first:

```bash
entire trail review list --status any
entire trail review 425
entire trail review comments 425
```

## Commands

### `entire trail review [<trail>]`

Shows the review dashboard. Defaults to the current branch's trail.

Flags:

- `--trail <number|id|branch>`: explicit trail selector
- `--status open,resolved,dismissed|any`
- `--severity high,medium,low`
- `--stale current,stale,any`
- `--include-dismissed`
- `--limit/-n <n>`
- `--offset <n>`
- `--json`

### `entire trail review list`

Lists trails in the current repo so a user can discover selectors.

```bash
entire trail review list --status any
entire trail review list --status in_review,open --limit 20
```

Human output includes number, id, status, branch, title, and updated time.

### `entire trail review start [<trail>]`

Starts or reuses an agent-native review for the target trail.

Flags:

- `--base-ref <ref>`
- `--head-ref <ref>`
- `--base-sha <sha>`
- `--head-sha <sha>`
- `--json`
- `--watch`

### `entire trail review comments [<trail>]`

Lists review findings. Uses the same list filters as the dashboard.

### `entire trail review comment add [<trail>]`

Creates a trail-scoped review finding. Defaults to the current branch's trail.

```bash
entire trail review comment add \
  --title "Potential nil dereference" \
  --body "This can panic when user is nil." \
  --severity high \
  --file internal/auth/session.go \
  --line 42 \
  --client-id "agent-run-123:finding-1"
```

Flags:

- `--title <text>`
- `--body/-m <text>`: required
- `--severity high,medium,low`
- `--confidence <0.0-1.0>`
- `--file <path>`
- `--line <n>` or `--start-line <n> [--end-line <n>]`
- `--client-id <id>`: recommended for agent idempotency
- `--patch <unified-diff>`
- `--instruction <text>`
- `--json`

`entire trail review comments add` is accepted as an alias for agents/users who think of findings as comments.

### `entire trail review show [<trail>] <comment-id>`

Shows one finding. Comment id prefixes are accepted when unambiguous.

### `entire trail review apply [<trail>] <comment-id>`

Applies supported `unified_diff` suggested changes.

Flags:

- `--check`: verify only; do not modify files
- `--resolve`: mark the finding resolved after applying

Safety behavior:

- verifies current `HEAD` matches the reviewed head when the API provides one
- rejects absolute paths, repository escapes, and `.git` metadata paths
- concatenates supported patches, checks once, then applies once

### Status commands

```bash
entire trail review resolve [<trail>] <comment-id> -m "fixed"
entire trail review dismiss [<trail>] <comment-id> -m "not applicable"
entire trail review reopen [<trail>] <comment-id> -m "rechecking"
```

### Verdict commands

```bash
entire trail review approve [<trail>] -m "looks good"
entire trail review request-changes [<trail>] -m "please address findings"
```

`request-changes` requires `--message`.

### `entire trail review watch [<trail>]`

Streams review Server-Sent Events.

Flags:

- `--json`: emit JSON lines
- `--show-pings`
- `--once`: open one SSE connection then exit

## Create-comment API

The CLI creates comments through a trail-scoped API endpoint so agents do not need to know a review id:

```http
POST /api/v1/trails/{trail_id}/reviews/comments
```

Example body:

```json
{
  "client_id": "agent-run-123:finding-7",
  "title": "Missing expiry skew handling",
  "body": "Token refresh should allow clock skew before treating the session as expired.",
  "severity": "high",
  "confidence": 0.94,
  "location": {
    "granularity": "line",
    "file_path": "src/auth/session.ts",
    "start_line": 88
  },
  "suggested_changes": [
    {
      "change_type": "manual_instruction",
      "instruction": "Allow a five minute skew before expiring the session."
    }
  ]
}
```

Use `client_id` for idempotency when agents retry the same finding.

# E2E examples

Manual end-to-end examples for workflows that touch real Entire services.

These are **not run by CI**. They are intended as copy/pasteable golden paths for release verification and debugging. Run them from a git repository with an `origin` remote that resolves to a repo with trails, and authenticate first with `entire login`.

## Trail review golden path

```bash
./e2e/examples/trail-review-golden-path.sh
```

Optional environment variables:

- `ENTIRE_BIN`: path to the CLI binary, defaults to `entire`
- `ENTIRE_TRAIL_REVIEW_SELECTOR`: trail number, id, or branch; defaults to the current branch's trail
- `ENTIRE_TRAIL_REVIEW_FILE`: file path for the example finding, defaults to `README.md`
- `ENTIRE_TRAIL_REVIEW_LINE`: line for the example finding, defaults to `1`

The script exercises the intended user/agent path:

1. discover trails
2. show dashboard for current branch/default target
3. start/reuse a review
4. create a trail-scoped comment with a `client_id`
5. list comments
6. show the created comment
7. resolve the created comment

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Golden path for manual trail-review CLI verification.
# Run from a git repo with an origin remote and an authenticated Entire CLI.

ENTIRE_BIN="${ENTIRE_BIN:-entire}"
TARGET_SELECTOR="${ENTIRE_TRAIL_REVIEW_SELECTOR:-}"
FINDING_FILE="${ENTIRE_TRAIL_REVIEW_FILE:-README.md}"
FINDING_LINE="${ENTIRE_TRAIL_REVIEW_LINE:-1}"
CLIENT_ID="trail-review-e2e:$(date +%s):$$"

target_args=()
if [[ -n "$TARGET_SELECTOR" ]]; then
  target_args+=("$TARGET_SELECTOR")
fi

run() {
  printf '\n$ %q' "$ENTIRE_BIN"
  printf ' %q' "$@"
  printf '\n'
  "$ENTIRE_BIN" "$@"
}

need() {
  if ! command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "missing required command: $1" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

need "$ENTIRE_BIN"
need jq

echo "Trail review golden path"
echo "Target: ${TARGET_SELECTOR:-current branch trail}"
echo "Finding location: ${FINDING_FILE}:${FINDING_LINE}"

run trail review list --status any --limit 10
run trail review "${target_args[@]}"
run trail review start "${target_args[@]}"

printf '\n$ %q' "$ENTIRE_BIN"
printf ' %q' trail review comment add "${target_args[@]}" \
  --json \
  --title "E2E review finding" \
  --body "Golden-path review finding created by the trail review E2E example." \
  --severity medium \
  --confidence 0.9 \
  --file "$FINDING_FILE" \
  --line "$FINDING_LINE" \
  --client-id "$CLIENT_ID"
printf '\n'

comment_json=$("$ENTIRE_BIN" trail review comment add "${target_args[@]}" \
  --json \
  --title "E2E review finding" \
  --body "Golden-path review finding created by the trail review E2E example." \
  --severity medium \
  --confidence 0.9 \
  --file "$FINDING_FILE" \
  --line "$FINDING_LINE" \
  --client-id "$CLIENT_ID")

printf '%s\n' "$comment_json" | jq .
comment_id=$(printf '%s\n' "$comment_json" | jq -r '.id')
if [[ -z "$comment_id" || "$comment_id" == "null" ]]; then
  echo "create comment response did not include .id" >&2
  exit 1
fi

run trail review comments "${target_args[@]}" --status any --include-dismissed
run trail review show "${target_args[@]}" "$comment_id"
run trail review resolve "${target_args[@]}" "$comment_id" -m "resolved by trail review golden-path e2e example"
run trail review comments "${target_args[@]}" --status any --include-dismissed

echo
printf 'Golden path complete. Created and resolved comment: %s\n' "$comment_id"

https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/425

## Summary
- Add `entire trail review` for agent-native review dashboards, finding lists/detail views, review start/watch, status updates, verdict submission, and unified-diff suggestion apply.
- Make the current branch's trail the default target everywhere; trail selectors are optional overrides and may be a number, trail id, or branch name.
- Add `entire trail review list` so users can discover trail numbers/ids/branches before selecting a trail.
- Add trail-scoped review-comment creation via CLI and API types: `POST /api/v1/trails/{trail_id}/reviews/comments`.
- Document the command usage in `docs/trail-review.md` and add manual golden-path e2e examples under `e2e/examples/`.

## Targeting model

All commands that accept `[<trail>]` default to the trail for the current git branch. Use a selector only when operating on another trail in the same repo.

A trail selector can be:

```text
425                       # trail number
#425                      # trail number with # prefix
trl_abc123                # trail id
feat/trail-review-cli     # branch name
```

Selectors can be positional or passed with `--trail`:

```bash
entire trail review
entire trail review 425
entire trail review --trail feat/trail-review-cli
entire trail review comments --trail trl_abc123
```

If `entire trail review` cannot resolve a current-branch trail, it falls back to printing the repo trail list so the user can pick a selector.

## Golden path

```bash
# Discover trails when needed.
entire trail review list --status any

# Work on the current branch's trail by default.
entire trail review
entire trail review start
entire trail review comments

# Agents/users can create findings without knowing a review id.
entire trail review comment add \
  --title "Missing expiry skew handling" \
  --body "Token refresh should allow clock skew before treating the session as expired." \
  --severity high \
  --confidence 0.94 \
  --file src/auth/session.ts \
  --line 88 \
  --client-id "agent-run-123:finding-7"

# Act on findings.
entire trail review show <comment-id>
entire trail review resolve <comment-id> -m "fixed in <sha>"
entire trail review watch
```

A runnable manual example is included at:

```bash
./e2e/examples/trail-review-golden-path.sh
```

## Command documentation

Full usage docs live in `docs/trail-review.md`.

### `entire trail review [<trail>]`

Shows the review dashboard for the current branch's trail, or the selected trail.

Flags: `--trail`, `--status`, `--severity`, `--stale`, `--include-dismissed`, `--limit/-n`, `--offset`, `--json`.

### `entire trail review list`

Lists reviewable trails in the current repo with number, id, status, branch, title, and updated time.

Flags: `--status`, `--limit/-n`, `--json`.

### `entire trail review start [<trail>]`

Starts or reuses an agent-native review for the target trail. Sends an `Idempotency-Key` derived from trail/base/head inputs.

Flags: `--base-ref`, `--head-ref`, `--base-sha`, `--head-sha`, `--json`, `--watch`.

### `entire trail review comments [<trail>]`

Lists review findings for the target trail. Uses the same filters as the dashboard.

Flags: `--trail`, `--status`, `--severity`, `--stale`, `--include-dismissed`, `--limit/-n`, `--offset`, `--json`.

### `entire trail review comment add [<trail>]`

Creates a review finding on the target trail. This is trail-scoped and does not require callers to know a review id.

Flags: `--title`, `--body/-m`, `--severity`, `--confidence`, `--file`, `--line`, `--start-line`, `--end-line`, `--client-id`, `--patch`, `--instruction`, `--json`.

`entire trail review comments add` is also accepted as an alias.

### `entire trail review show [<trail>] <comment-id>`

Shows one finding. Prefix matching is supported when unambiguous.

### `entire trail review apply [<trail>] <comment-id>`

Applies supported `unified_diff` suggestions.

Safety behavior:
- verifies current `HEAD` matches the reviewed head when the API provides one
- rejects absolute paths, repository escapes, and `.git` metadata paths
- concatenates all supported unified-diff patches, checks once, then applies once

Flags: `--check`, `--resolve`.

### Status and verdict commands

```bash
entire trail review resolve [<trail>] <comment-id> -m "fixed"
entire trail review dismiss [<trail>] <comment-id> -m "not applicable"
entire trail review reopen [<trail>] <comment-id> -m "rechecking"
entire trail review approve [<trail>] -m "looks good"
entire trail review request-changes [<trail>] -m "please address findings"
```

`request-changes` requires `--message`.

### `entire trail review watch [<trail>]`

Streams review SSE events. Flags: `--json`, `--show-pings`, `--once`.

## API shape added for comment creation

```http
POST /api/v1/trails/{trail_id}/reviews/comments
```

Example request:

```json
{
  "client_id": "agent-run-123:finding-7",
  "title": "Missing expiry skew handling",
  "body": "Token refresh should allow clock skew before treating the session as expired.",
  "severity": "high",
  "confidence": 0.94,
  "location": {
    "granularity": "line",
    "file_path": "src/auth/session.ts",
    "start_line": 88
  },
  "suggested_changes": [
    {
      "change_type": "manual_instruction",
      "instruction": "Allow a five minute skew before expiring the session."
    }
  ]
}
```

Use `client_id` for idempotency when agents retry the same finding.

## Tests
- `env -u PI_CODING_AGENT mise exec -- go test ./cmd/entire/cli ./cmd/entire/cli/api`
- `env -u PI_CODING_AGENT mise exec -- go test ./...`
- `mise exec -- golangci-lint run`
- `git diff --check`

Note: e2e examples under `e2e/examples/` are manual service-backed scripts and were not run automatically.

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/425
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary
- Add `entire trail review` for agent-native review dashboards, finding lists/detail views, review start/watch, status updates, verdict submission, and unified-diff suggestion apply.
- Make the current branch's trail the default target everywhere; trail selectors are optional overrides and may be a number, trail id, or branch name.
- Add `entire trail review list` so users can discover trail numbers/ids/branches before selecting a trail.
- Add trail-scoped review-comment creation via CLI and API types: `POST /api/v1/trails/{trail_id}/reviews/comments`.
- Document the command usage in `docs/trail-review.md` and add manual golden-path e2e examples under `e2e/examples/`.

## Targeting model

All commands that accept `[<trail>]` default to the trail for the current git branch. Use a selector only when operating on another trail in the same repo.

A trail selector can be:

```text
425                       # trail number
#425                      # trail number with # prefix
trl_abc123                # trail id
feat/trail-review-cli     # branch name
```

Selectors can be positional or passed with `--trail`:

```bash
entire trail review
entire trail review 425
entire trail review --trail feat/trail-review-cli
entire trail review comments --trail trl_abc123
```

If `entire trail review` cannot resolve a current-branch trail, it falls back to printing the repo trail list so the user can pick a selector.

## Golden path

```bash
# Discover trails when needed.
entire trail review list --status any

# Work on the current branch's trail by default.
entire trail review
entire trail review start
entire trail review comments

# Agents/users can create findings without knowing a review id.
entire trail review comment add \
  --title "Missing expiry skew handling" \
  --body "Token refresh should allow clock skew before treating the session as expired." \
  --severity high \
  --confidence 0.94 \
  --file src/auth/session.ts \
  --line 88 \
  --client-id "agent-run-123:finding-7"

# Act on findings.
entire trail review show <comment-id>
entire trail review resolve <comment-id> -m "fixed in <sha>"
entire trail review watch
```

A runnable manual example is included at:

```bash
./e2e/examples/trail-review-golden-path.sh
```

## Command documentation

Full usage docs live in `docs/trail-review.md`.

### `entire trail review [<trail>]`

Shows the review dashboard for the current branch's trail, or the selected trail.

Flags: `--trail`, `--status`, `--severity`, `--stale`, `--include-dismissed`, `--limit/-n`, `--offset`, `--json`.

### `entire trail review list`

arguments.content:
# Trail review CLI

`entire trail review` works on the trail for your current branch by default. You only need a selector when operating on another trail in the same repository.

Use the existing trail list command to discover selectors:

```bash
entire trail list --status any
```

Trail selectors can be:

- trail number: `425`
- trail number with hash prefix: `#425`
- trail id: `trl_abc123`
- branch name: `feat/token-refresh`

Because most shells treat an unquoted `#425` as a comment, pass hash-prefixed selectors as one of:

```bash
entire trail review '#425'
entire trail review --trail '#425'
entire trail review --trail=#425
```

Selectors can be positional or passed with `--trail`:

```bash
entire trail review
entire trail review 425
entire trail review --trail feat/token-refresh
entire trail review comments --trail trl_abc123
```

If no current-branch trail can be resolved, `entire trail review` prints the regular trail list so you can pick one.

## Golden path

```bash
# 1. Discover trails if you are not on the branch already.
entire trail list --status any

# 2. Show review status for the current branch's trail.
entire trail review

# 3. Start or reuse an agent-native review for the current HEAD.
entire trail review start

# 4. List findings for the current branch's trail.
entire trail review comments

# 5. Create a review finding on the current branch's trail.
entire trail review comment add \
  --title "Missing expiry skew handling" \
  --body "Token refresh should allow clock skew before treating the session as expired." \
  --severity high \
  --confidence 0.94 \
  --file src/auth/session.ts \
  --line 88 \
  --client-id "agent-run-123:finding-7"

# 6. Inspect, resolve, or dismiss a finding.
entire trail review show <comment-id>
entire trail review resolve <comment-id> -m "fixed in <sha>"
entire trail review dismiss <comment-id> -m "not applicable"

# 7. Watch review events.
entire trail review watch
```

A runnable manual version of this flow lives at `e2e/examples/trail-review-golden-path.sh`.

## Command output examples

### `entire trail list --status any`

Discovery uses the existing trail list command. Rows include the selector users need.

```text
  Recent trails · 2

  In review · 1

  NUM  BRANCH                  TITLE                   AUTHOR  UPDATED
  425  feat/trail-review-cli   Add trail review CLI    dipree  3m ago

  Open · 1

  NUM  BRANCH                  TITLE                   AUTHOR  UPDATED
  421  fix/auth-refresh        Fix token refresh       dipree  2d ago
```

### `entire trail review [<trail>]`

```text
Trail #425  Add trail review CLI
Status: in_review   Branch: feat/trail-review-cli   Base: main
ID: trl_123

Open findings: 3  high 1  medium 1  low 1
Resolved: 2        Dismissed: 1     Stale: 0

High
  H src/auth/session.ts:88   cmt_high_123   Missing expiry skew handling

Medium
  M src/api/client.ts:141   cmt_med_456   Retry loop can spin forever

Low
  L src/ui/Login.tsx:52   cmt_low_789   Error state is swallowed

Actions:
  entire trail review show <comment-id>
  entire trail review comment add -m "finding body" --file path --line 42
  entire trail review apply <comment-id> --resolve
  entire trail review resolve <comment-id> -m "fixed in <sha>"
  entire trail review dismiss <comment-id> -m "not applicable"
  entire trail review watch
```

If no current-branch trail is found:

```text
No trail found for the current branch; showing trails in this repo.

  Recent trails · 2

  NUM  BRANCH                  TITLE                   AUTHOR  UPDATED
  425  feat/trail-review-cli   Add trail review CLI    dipree  3m ago
  421  fix/auth-refresh        Fix token refresh       dipree  2d ago
```

With `--json`, output is an object containing `trail`, `counts`, `comments`, and `has_more`.

### `entire trail review start [<trail>]`

```text
Started review rvw_123 for trail #425 (Add trail review CLI)
  Code version: cv_123
  Base: 1a2b3c4d5e6f
  Head: 9f8e7d6c5b4a

Next:
  entire trail review watch 425
  entire trail review comments 425
```

With `--json`, output is the API start response.

### `entire trail review comments [<trail>]`

```text
ID            SEV     STATUS  LOCATION                 TITLE
cmt_high_123  high    open    src/auth/session.ts:88   Missing expiry skew handling
cmt_med_456   medium  open    src/api/client.ts:141    Retry loop can spin forever
```

When more pages exist:

```text
More findings available; rerun with --offset for the next page.
```

When no findings match:

```text
No review findings found.
```

### `entire trail review comment add [<trail>]`

```text
Created review comment cmt_high_123 on trail #425 (Add trail review CLI)
Status:   open
Severity: high
Location: src/auth/session.ts:88
Title:    Missing expiry skew handling
```

Example command:

```bash
entire trail review comment add \
  --title "Potential nil dereference" \
  --body "This can panic when user is nil." \
  --severity high \
  --confidence 0.91 \
  --file internal/auth/session.go \
  --line 42 \
  --client-id "agent-run-123:finding-1"
```

`entire trail review comments add` is accepted as an alias.

### `entire trail review show [<trail>] <comment-id>`

```text
Comment:  cmt_high_123
Review:   rvw_123
Status:   open
Severity: high
Confidence: 0.94
Location: src/auth/session.ts:88
Title:    Missing expiry skew handling

Token refresh should allow clock skew before treating the session as expired.

Suggested changes:
- sug_123 (manual_instruction)
  instruction: Allow a five minute skew before expiring the session.
```

### `entire trail review apply [<trail>] <comment-id>`

Successful apply:

```text
Applied 1 suggested change(s).
```

Check-only:

```text
1 suggested change(s) apply cleanly.
```

With `--resolve`:

```text
Applied 1 suggested change(s).
Updated comment cmt_high_123: open → resolved
```

Unsupported suggestion types are skipped before applying supported patches:

```text
Skipping suggested change sug_manual (manual_instruction): only unified_diff patches are supported.
```

### `entire trail review resolve [<trail>] <comment-id>`

```text
Updated comment cmt_high_123: open → resolved
```

If `--message` is omitted, the status reason defaults to `Resolved via Entire CLI`.

### `entire trail review dismiss [<trail>] <comment-id>`

```text
Updated comment cmt_low_789: open → dismissed
```

If `--message` is omitted, the status reason defaults to `Dismissed via Entire CLI`.

### `entire trail review reopen [<trail>] <comment-id>`

```text
Updated comment cmt_low_789: dismissed → open
```

If `--message` is omitted, the status reason defaults to `Reopened via Entire CLI`.

### `entire trail review approve [<trail>]`

```text
APPROVE submitted by dipree on 9f8e7d6c5b4a
```

### `entire trail review request-changes [<trail>]`

```text
REQUEST_CHANGES submitted by dipree on 9f8e7d6c5b4a
```

If `--message` is omitted:

```text
request-changes requires --message
```

### `entire trail review watch [<trail>]`

The watch banner is written to stderr, and events are written to stdout.

```text
Watching trail #425 (gh/entireio/cli, id trl_123) — Ctrl+C to stop
● connected to trail trl_123 after event 17
[12:34:56] session started by agent:reviewer (code version cv_123)
[12:35:04] comment created by agent:reviewer on src/auth/session.ts (high) — cmt_high_123
[12:35:10] session ended by agent:reviewer (done)
```

With `--json`, each SSE event is emitted as one JSON line:

```json
{"event":"comment.created","data":{"id":"18","trail_id":"trl_123","event_type":"comment.created"}}
```

## Flags

### Shared target flag

- `--trail <number|id|branch>`: explicit trail selector. Defaults to the current branch's trail.

### Shared finding-list flags

- `--status open,resolved,dismissed|any`
- `--severity high,medium,low`
- `--stale current,stale,any`
- `--include-dismissed`
- `--limit/-n <n>`
- `--offset <n>`
- `--json`

### `comment add` flags

- `--title <text>`
- `--body/-m <text>`: required
- `--severity high,medium,low`
- `--confidence <0.0-1.0>`
- `--file <path>`
- `--line <n>` or `--start-line <n> [--end-line <n>]`
- `--client-id <id>`: recommended for agent idempotency
- `--patch <unified-diff>`
- `--instruction <text>`
- `--json`

## Create-comment API

The CLI creates comments through a trail-scoped API endpoint so agents do not need to know a review id:

```http
POST /api/v1/trails/{trail_id}/reviews/comments
```

Example body:

```json
{
  "client_id": "agent-run-123:finding-7",
  "title": "Missing expiry skew handling",
  "body": "Token refresh should allow clock skew before treating the session as expired.",
  "severity": "high",
  "confidence": 0.94,
  "location": {
    "granularity": "line",
    "file_path": "src/auth/session.ts",
    "start_line": 88
  },
  "suggested_changes": [
    {
      "change_type": "manual_instruction",
      "instruction": "Allow a five minute skew before expiring the session."
    }
  ]
}
```

Use `client_id` for idempotency when agents retry the same finding.

## Summary
- Add `entire trail review` for agent-native review dashboards, finding lists/detail views, review start/watch, status updates, verdict submission, and unified-diff suggestion apply.
- Make the current branch's trail the default target everywhere; trail selectors are optional overrides and may be a number, `#`-prefixed number, trail id, or branch name.

## Targeting model

All commands that accept `[<trail>]` default to the trail for the current git branch. Use a selector only when operating on another trail in the same repo.

Selectors can be:

425                       # trail number

Because most shells treat unquoted `#425` as a comment, use one of:

Selectors can be positional or passed with `--trail`:

If `entire trail review` cannot resolve a current-branch trail, it falls back to printing the regular trail list so the user can pick a selector.

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/425
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary
- Add `entire trail review` for agent-native review dashboards, finding lists/detail, review start/watch, status updates, and unified-diff suggestion apply.
- Default every review command to the current branch's trail; explicit selectors are only overrides.
- Support selectors by trail number, trail id, or branch name. No `#` prefix support; use bare numbers like `425`.
- Use existing `entire trail list --status any` for discovery; trail list rows now show `NUM` and `TITLE`.
- Add trail-scoped comment creation via `POST /api/v1/trails/{trail_id}/reviews/comments` so agents do not need a review id.
- Add manual golden-path e2e example: `e2e/examples/trail-review-golden-path.sh`.

## Targeting

```bash
entire trail review                  # current branch's trail
entire trail review 425              # by number
entire trail review trl_abc123       # by id
entire trail review feat/my-branch   # by branch
entire trail review --trail 425      # explicit flag form
```

If the current branch has no trail, `entire trail review` falls back to `entire trail list --status any` output.

## Golden path

```bash
entire trail list --status any
entire trail review
entire trail review start
entire trail review comments
entire trail review comment add \
  --title "Missing expiry skew handling" \
  --body "Token refresh should allow clock skew before treating the session as expired." \
  --severity high \
  --confidence 0.94 \
  --file src/auth/session.ts \
  --line 88 \
  --client-id "agent-run-123:finding-7"
entire trail review show <comment-id>
entire trail review resolve <comment-id> -m "fixed in <sha>"
entire trail review watch
```

## Output examples

### `entire trail list --status any`

```text
  Recent trails · 2

  Open · 1

  NUM  BRANCH                  TITLE                   AUTHOR  UPDATED
  421  fix/auth-refresh        Fix token refresh       dipree  2d ago

  In review · 1

  NUM  BRANCH                  TITLE                   AUTHOR  UPDATED
  425  feat/trail-review-cli   Add trail review CLI    dipree  3m ago
```

### `entire trail review`

```text
Trail #425  Add trail review CLI
Status: in_review   Branch: feat/trail-review-cli   Base: main
ID: trl_123

Open findings: 3  high 1  medium 1  low 1
Resolved: 2        Dismissed: 1     Stale: 0

High
  H src/auth/session.ts:88   cmt_high_123   Missing expiry skew handling

Actions:
  entire trail review show <comment-id>
  entire trail review comment add -m "finding body" --file path --line 42
  entire trail review apply <comment-id> --resolve
  entire trail review resolve <comment-id> -m "fixed in <sha>"
  entire trail review dismiss <comment-id> -m "not applicable"
  entire trail review watch
```

### No current-branch trail fallback

```text
No trail found for the current branch; showing trails in this repo.

  Recent trails · 2

  NUM  BRANCH                  TITLE                   AUTHOR  UPDATED
  421  fix/auth-refresh        Fix token refresh       dipree  2d ago
  425  feat/trail-review-cli   Add trail review CLI    dipree  3m ago
```

### `entire trail review start`

```text
Started review rvw_123 for trail #425 (Add trail review CLI)
  Code version: cv_123
  Base: 1a2b3c4d5e6f
  Head: 9f8e7d6c5b4a

Next:
  entire trail review watch 425
  entire trail review comments 425
```

### `entire trail review comments`

```text
ID            SEV     STATUS  LOCATION                 TITLE
cmt_high_123  high    open    src/auth/session.ts:88   Missing expiry skew handling
cmt_med_456   medium  open    src/api/client.ts:141    Retry loop can spin forever
```

### `entire trail review comment add`

```text
Created review comment cmt_high_123 on trail #425 (Add trail review CLI)
Status:   open
Severity: high
Location: src/auth/session.ts:88
Title:    Missing expiry skew handling
```

### `entire trail review show <comment-id>`

```text
Comment:  cmt_high_123
Review:   rvw_123
Status:   open
Severity: high
Confidence: 0.94
Location: src/auth/session.ts:88
Title:    Missing expiry skew handling

Token refresh should allow clock skew before treating the session as expired.
```

### `entire trail review apply <comment-id>`

```text
Applied 1 suggested change(s).
```

With `--check`:

```text
1 suggested change(s) apply cleanly.
```

With `--resolve`:

```text
Applied 1 suggested change(s).
Updated comment cmt_high_123: open → resolved
```

### Status commands

```text
$ entire trail review resolve <comment-id> -m "fixed in abc123"
Updated comment cmt_high_123: open → resolved

$ entire trail review dismiss <comment-id> -m "not applicable"
Updated comment cmt_low_789: open → dismissed

$ entire trail review reopen <comment-id> -m "rechecking"
Updated comment cmt_low_789: dismissed → open
```

### `entire trail review watch`

```text
Watching trail #425 (gh/entireio/cli, id trl_123) — Ctrl+C to stop
● connected to trail trl_123 after event 17
[12:34:56] session started by agent:reviewer (code version cv_123)
[12:35:04] comment created by agent:reviewer on src/auth/session.ts (high) — cmt_high_123
[12:35:10] session ended by agent:reviewer (done)
```

## API shape added for comment creation

```http
POST /api/v1/trails/{trail_id}/reviews/comments
```

```json
{
  "client_id": "agent-run-123:finding-7",
  "title": "Missing expiry skew handling",
  "body": "Token refresh should allow clock skew before treating the session as expired.",
  "severity": "high",
  "confidence": 0.94,
  "location": {
    "granularity": "line",
    "file_path": "src/auth/session.ts",
    "start_line": 88
  }
}
```

- `env -u PI_CODING_AGENT mise exec -- go test ./...`
- `mise exec -- golangci-lint run`
- `git diff --check`

Manual e2e example was added but not run automatically because it hits real services.

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/425
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary
- Add `entire trail review` for agent-native review findings: dashboard, comments list/detail, create comment, status updates, patch apply, and SSE watch.
- Default review commands to the current branch's trail; explicit selectors are only overrides (`425`, `trl_abc123`, or `feat/my-branch`). No `#425` selector support.
- Reuse existing `entire trail list --status any` for discovery. This PR only improves that output with `NUM` and `TITLE` columns.
- Add trail-scoped comment creation via `POST /api/v1/trails/{trail_id}/reviews/comments` so agents do not need a review id.
- Add manual golden-path e2e example: `e2e/examples/trail-review-golden-path.sh`.

## Golden path

```bash
entire trail list --status any
entire trail review
entire trail review comments
entire trail review comment add \
  --title "Missing expiry skew handling" \
  --body "Token refresh should allow clock skew before treating the session as expired." \
  --severity high \
  --confidence 0.94 \
  --file src/auth/session.ts \
  --line 88 \
  --client-id "agent-run-123:finding-7"
entire trail review show <comment-id>
entire trail review resolve <comment-id> -m "fixed in <sha>"
entire trail review watch
```

## Making a code suggestion

Attach a unified diff when creating the finding:

```bash
git diff > suggestion.diff
entire trail review comment add \
  --title "Handle missing token" \
  --body "This path should return a typed auth error." \
  --severity medium \
  --file src/auth/session.ts \
  --line 88 \
  --patch-file suggestion.diff \
  --client-id "agent-run-123:finding-8"
```

`--patch-file -` reads the diff from stdin. `--patch` is also available for inline diffs. Users can later run:

```bash
entire trail review apply <comment-id> --check
entire trail review apply <comment-id> --resolve
```

## About `entire trail review start`

`start` is optional and not part of the normal read/post/respond loop above. It exists to explicitly request or rerun an automated review and pin the base/head refs and SHAs the reviewer should analyze. Listing comments and posting trail-scoped comments do not require it.

## Output examples

### `entire trail list --status any`

```text
  Recent trails · 2

  Open · 1

  NUM  BRANCH                  TITLE                   AUTHOR  UPDATED
  421  fix/auth-refresh        Fix token refresh       dipree  2d ago

  In review · 1

  NUM  BRANCH                  TITLE                   AUTHOR  UPDATED
  425  feat/trail-review-cli   Add trail review CLI    dipree  3m ago
```

### `entire trail review`

```text
Trail #425  Add trail review CLI
Status: in_review   Branch: feat/trail-review-cli   Base: main
ID: trl_123

Open findings: 3  high 1  medium 1  low 1
Resolved: 2        Dismissed: 1     Stale: 0

High
  H src/auth/session.ts:88   cmt_high_123   Missing expiry skew handling

Actions:
  entire trail review show <comment-id>
  entire trail review comment add -m "finding body" --file path --line 42
  entire trail review apply <comment-id> --resolve
  entire trail review resolve <comment-id> -m "fixed in <sha>"
  entire trail review dismiss <comment-id> -m "not applicable"
  entire trail review watch
```

### No current-branch trail fallback

```text
No trail found for the current branch; showing trails in this repo.

  Recent trails · 2

  NUM  BRANCH                  TITLE                   AUTHOR  UPDATED
  421  fix/auth-refresh        Fix token refresh       dipree  2d ago
  425  feat/trail-review-cli   Add trail review CLI    dipree  3m ago
```

### `entire trail review comments`

```text
ID            SEV     STATUS  LOCATION                 TITLE
cmt_high_123  high    open    src/auth/session.ts:88   Missing expiry skew handling
cmt_med_456   medium  open    src/api/client.ts:141    Retry loop can spin forever
```

### `entire trail review comment add`

```text
Created review comment cmt_high_123 on trail #425 (Add trail review CLI)
Status:   open
Severity: high
Location: src/auth/session.ts:88
Title:    Missing expiry skew handling
```

### `entire trail review show <comment-id>`

```text
Comment:  cmt_high_123
Review:   rvw_123
Status:   open
Severity: high
Confidence: 0.94
Location: src/auth/session.ts:88
Title:    Missing expiry skew handling

Token refresh should allow clock skew before treating the session as expired.
```

### `entire trail review apply <comment-id>`

```text
Applied 1 suggested change(s).
```

With `--check`:

```text
1 suggested change(s) apply cleanly.
```

With `--resolve`:

```text
Applied 1 suggested change(s).
Updated comment cmt_high_123: open → resolved
```

### Status commands

```text
$ entire trail review resolve <comment-id> -m "fixed in abc123"
Updated comment cmt_high_123: open → resolved

$ entire trail review dismiss <comment-id> -m "not applicable"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Golden path for manual trail-review CLI verification.
# Run from a git repo with an origin remote and an authenticated Entire CLI.

ENTIRE_BIN="${ENTIRE_BIN:-entire}"
TARGET_SELECTOR="${ENTIRE_TRAIL_REVIEW_SELECTOR:-}"
FINDING_FILE="${ENTIRE_TRAIL_REVIEW_FILE:-README.md}"
FINDING_LINE="${ENTIRE_TRAIL_REVIEW_LINE:-1}"
CLIENT_ID="trail-review-e2e:$(date +%s):$$"

target_args=()
if [[ -n "$TARGET_SELECTOR" ]]; then
  target_args+=("$TARGET_SELECTOR")
fi

run() {
  printf '\n$ %q' "$ENTIRE_BIN"
  printf ' %q' "$@"
  printf '\n'
  "$ENTIRE_BIN" "$@"
}

need() {
  if ! command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "missing required command: $1" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

need "$ENTIRE_BIN"
need jq

echo "Trail review golden path"
echo "Target: ${TARGET_SELECTOR:-current branch trail}"
echo "Finding location: ${FINDING_FILE}:${FINDING_LINE}"

run trail list --status any --limit 10
run trail review "${target_args[@]}"

printf '\n$ %q' "$ENTIRE_BIN"
printf ' %q' trail review comment add "${target_args[@]}" \
  --json \
  --title "E2E review finding" \
  --body "Golden-path review finding created by the trail review E2E example." \
  --severity medium \
  --confidence 0.9 \
  --file "$FINDING_FILE" \
  --line "$FINDING_LINE" \
  --client-id "$CLIENT_ID"
printf '\n'

comment_json=$("$ENTIRE_BIN" trail review comment add "${target_args[@]}" \
  --json \
  --title "E2E review finding" \
  --body "Golden-path review finding created by the trail review E2E example." \
  --severity medium \
  --confidence 0.9 \
  --file "$FINDING_FILE" \
  --line "$FINDING_LINE" \
  --client-id "$CLIENT_ID")

printf '%s\n' "$comment_json" | jq .
comment_id=$(printf '%s\n' "$comment_json" | jq -r '.id')
if [[ -z "$comment_id" || "$comment_id" == "null" ]]; then
  echo "create comment response did not include .id" >&2
  exit 1
fi

run trail review comments "${target_args[@]}" --status any --include-dismissed
run trail review show "${target_args[@]}" "$comment_id"
run trail review resolve "${target_args[@]}" "$comment_id" -m "resolved by trail review golden-path e2e example"
run trail review comments "${target_args[@]}" --status any --include-dismissed

echo
printf 'Golden path complete. Created and resolved comment: %s\n' "$comment_id"

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/425
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary
- Add `entire trail review` for agent-native review findings: dashboard, comments list/detail, create comment, status updates, patch apply, and SSE watch.
- Default review commands to the current branch's trail; explicit selectors are only overrides (`425`, `trl_abc123`, or `feat/my-branch`).
- Reuse existing `entire trail list --status any` for discovery; this PR only improves list output with `NUM` and `TITLE` columns.
- Add trail-scoped comment creation via `POST /api/v1/trails/{trail_id}/reviews/comments` so agents do not need a review id.
- Add manual golden-path e2e example: `e2e/examples/trail-review-golden-path.sh`.

## Golden path

```bash
entire trail list --status any
entire trail review
entire trail review comments
entire trail review comment add \
  --title "Missing expiry skew handling" \
  --body "Token refresh should allow clock skew before treating the session as expired." \
  --severity high \
  --confidence 0.94 \
  --file src/auth/session.ts \
  --line 88 \
  --client-id "agent-run-123:finding-7"
entire trail review show <comment-id>
entire trail review resolve <comment-id> -m "fixed in <sha>"
entire trail review watch
```

## Making a code suggestion

Attach a unified diff when creating the finding:

```bash
git diff > suggestion.diff
entire trail review comment add \
  --title "Handle missing token" \
  --body "This path should return a typed auth error." \
  --severity medium \
  --file src/auth/session.ts \
  --line 88 \
  --patch-file suggestion.diff \
  --client-id "agent-run-123:finding-8"
```

`--patch-file -` reads the diff from stdin. `--patch` is also available for inline diffs. Users can later run:

```bash
entire trail review apply <comment-id> --check
entire trail review apply <comment-id> --resolve
```

## Output examples

### `entire trail list --status any`

Status: in_review   Branch: feat/trail-review-cli   Base: main
ID: trl_123

Open findings: 3  high 1  medium 1  low 1
Resolved: 2        Dismissed: 1     Stale: 0

High
  H src/auth/session.ts:88   cmt_high_123   Missing expiry skew handling

Actions:
  entire trail review show <comment-id>
  entire trail review comment add -m "finding body" --file path --line 42
  entire trail review apply <comment-id> --resolve
  entire trail review resolve <comment-id> -m "fixed in <sha>"
  entire trail review dismiss <comment-id> -m "not applicable"
  entire trail review watch
```

### No current-branch trail fallback

No trail found for the current branch; showing trails in this repo.

  Recent trails · 2

  NUM  BRANCH                  TITLE                   AUTHOR  UPDATED
  421  fix/auth-refresh        Fix token refresh       dipree  2d ago

I’m thinking about the user’s question regarding whether it's a best practice to use a list command for comments followed by a single comment command in a CLI. They mention "comments" as plural and "comment add" as singular, which is intriguing!  

I could reference existing conventions like "gh pr view/list" and "git branch." It seems that keeping the resource noun singular for operations might be a clearer structure. I could suggest using `comment` for all commands to keep things consistent and simple.

I’m considering another option: keeping `comments` as an alias for ease, while primary documentation should use `comment list`. The user's question is about best practices for CLI commands regarding pluralization and singularity.  

In evaluating CLI patterns, it's clear that consistency is key. It’s usually best to choose either singular or plural for resource namespaces, rather than mixing them. For example, the Cobra/CLI prefers verb commands like `review comments` and `review comment add`. GitHub’s approach does show some variance with commands like `gh pr comment`. I’ll just have to think this through more!

I’m thinking about proposing a command grammar for better clarity. One option I'm considering is:  

- `entire trail review comments` for a list,  
- `entire trail review comment <id>` for showing an individual comment, although that could be a bit ambiguous.  
- Then there’s `entire trail review comment add` for adding a new comment.  

I think this structure might work well, but I need to make sure I communicate clearly to avoid confusion with the `<id>` presentation. Let’s optimize this!

**Rethinking terminology for clarity**

I’m exploring how to enhance the user experience with the review actions. Instead of using "comment," maybe "findings" fits better since the feature calls them "agent findings," while the API uses "comments." This consistency might improve the mental model for users. 

I think concise commands like “entire trail review findings” or “finding show/add/resolve” could be clearer. However, the API's terminology relies on "comments" since that’s what users are asking about. Balancing user language with technical terminology is tricky!

**Exploring CLI best practices**

I'm considering best practices for naming conventions in command-line interfaces (CLIs). In the current CLI, using `trail list` followed by `trail` or `trail update` keeps the "list" verb explicit, while using "comments" as a bare plural feels inconsistent. 

Looking at other CLIs, like `gh issue list` or `kubectl get pods`, they generally use singular nouns with verbs. Consistency seems key, with a preference for one clear noun plus a verb, though plural nouns can serve as useful aliases for convenience!

**Refining command naming for clarity**

I’m thinking about how to avoid confusion with terms like `comments` for a list and `comment add` for creating entries. I want to set canonical commands like: 

- `entire trail review comment list [<trail>]`
- `entire trail review comment show [<trail>] <id>`, and others.

I might keep shorter aliases but I'm wondering if "comment" feels too technical. Perhaps using "finding" instead could align better with the dashboard's "agent findings." So maybe I can keep "comments" as an API-compatible alias while clarifying the user-facing terms!

content.text:
Usually no. Better practice is one consistent resource namespace.

Current mixed shape is a bit awkward:

```bash
entire trail review comments        # list
entire trail review comment add     # create one
entire trail review show <id>       # show one
```

Better canonical shape:

```bash
entire trail review comment list
entire trail review comment show <comment-id>
entire trail review comment add ...
entire trail review comment resolve <comment-id>
entire trail review comment dismiss <comment-id>
entire trail review comment reopen <comment-id>
entire trail review comment apply <comment-id>
```

Then aliases can exist for ergonomics:

```bash
entire trail review comments        # alias for comment list
entire trail review show <id>       # alias for comment show
entire trail review resolve <id>    # alias for comment resolve
```

This matches common CLI patterns better: resource + verb, e.g. `gh issue list/view/create`, `kubectl get/describe`, etc.

One caveat: “comment” may be API language while the UI says “finding.” If the user-facing concept is finding, then even better:

```bash
entire trail review finding list
entire trail review finding show <id>
entire trail review finding add ...
entire trail review finding resolve <id>
```

But if API/product calls them review comments, use `comment`. My recommendation: make `comment list/show/add/...` canonical and keep shorter old forms as aliases if desired.
We can do "finding" and drop the "review" as well?
